metaDescription: Six thick seat riser cushions compared on height, foam layers, size, non-slip bases and washable covers to help raise a low or sunken chair.
introParagraphs: A seat riser cushion is the simplest fix for a chair that sits too low or has sunk with age. It adds several inches of firm foam under you, so the seat height starts closer to your knee line and the rise to standing is shorter. There is no motor, no spring and nothing to charge, which is both the appeal and the limit: a riser raises the seat but it does not lift you as you stand.

This lineup covers six dual-layer foam cushions from HAVARGO, Hem Dgpsy, Acxseo, MABOZOO, Zantle and TANYOO. Thickness runs from 4 inches on the Zantle to 6 inches on the Acxseo and MABOZOO, and three of them measure 20 by 20 by 5 inches. We evaluated each one from the details on its product page, noting foam structure, non-slip bases, cover care and the maker's own sizing figures. We left out a car booster pad that is aimed at driving visibility.

Height is a real safety variable. A riser that is too thick leaves your feet dangling or tilts you back, and a cushion that slides on the seat can be a fall risk. Check the chair first, keep your feet flat after the rise, and ask a clinician or occupational therapist to confirm the height if you have balance concerns. Nothing here is medical advice or a claim of medical benefit.

products.name: HAVARGO 20x20x5 Inch Dual-Layer Recliner Cushion

specList.label: Layers
specList.value: 2.5 in firm foam plus 2.5 in soft layer

products.description:
The HAVARGO is a 20 by 20 by 5 inch cushion built from two layers. The lower 2.5 inches is a firm, supportive foam, and the upper 2.5 inches is a soft layer with shredded memory foam in the top. Silicone particles on the bottom grip the seat, and the cover opens with a large zipper whose pull is protected from wear.

The firm base is what holds the height. The soft top layer is what makes the cushion tolerable for a long sit. The maker describes it for recliners and armchairs, and it is also listed for couches, sofas and rocker chairs. Because the cushion is 20 inches square, it needs a seat wide enough to hold it without the corners hanging over.

The cushion ships compressed and the page asks for 24 hours to expand to full height, so do not judge the height out of the box. Compared with the Zantle at 4 inches it adds an extra inch, and compared with the MABOZOO at 6 inches it adds less height but gives a larger footprint. If you want a balanced, general-purpose riser for a recliner or armchair, this is the safest pick.

products.name: Hem Dgpsy 20x20x5 Inch Recliner Seat Cushion
products.description:
The Hem Dgpsy is the same 20 by 20 by 5 inch size as the HAVARGO, with a different build. The top layer combines shredded memory foam and polyester fiberfill, and a supportive foam pad underneath is meant to resist flattening. The maker says it adds about 5 inches of height to low or sunken seats, and silicone grip dots cover the entire bottom.

The standout is the removable waterproof cover, which protects the foam from spills, oil, dust and moisture. The page says to hand wash the cover in warm water and not to machine wash it, which is a real limit if you like to throw everything in the washer. The cushion can double as a thick floor cushion, though that is a secondary use.

The fiberfill-and-shred top is softer than a solid foam block, so check that the base pad still holds your height after a few weeks. Compared with the HAVARGO it has the better spill protection, and compared with the TANYOO it limits you to hand washing. If you share a chair with spills, pets or a lot of use, the waterproof cover is the reason to choose it.

products.name: TANYOO 20x20x5 Inch Recliner Seat Cushion

specList.label: Cover
specList.value: Zipped, hand or cold machine wash

products.description:
The TANYOO is a 20 by 20 by 5 inch cushion with an upper layer of soft shredded memory foam and a lower layer of solid high-density foam. Textured silicone dots on the bottom grip the seat. The maker describes it as a replacement for a sagging recliner cushion and a help for getting up.

The cover zips off and can be washed by hand or in cold water in the machine, with no ironing or bleach. The packaging detail is useful: the foam arrives vacuum-bagged and flat, and the page suggests a low-heat steamer or hair dryer to speed fluffing. That tells you to expect an initial wait before it reaches its full height.

The solid lower layer is the part that matters for height retention, because a loose-fill base would flatten faster. Compared with the Hem Dgpsy it has an easier cover to wash, and compared with the HAVARGO it offers the same size at a similar structure. If easy laundering is a priority for a chair that is used every day, this is the practical choice.

products.name: Acxseo 6 Inch Extra Thick Memory Foam Seat Cushion
products.description:
The Acxseo is the thickest cushion here at a stated 6 inches, tied with the MABOZOO. It is a two-layer high-density memory foam build with a breathable, water-resistant cover that removes for cleaning. A built-in side handle makes it easy to carry between chairs, and the non-slip bottom is meant to keep it from sliding.

Six inches is a lot of height, which suits a very low chair but is too much for many seats. The page lists uses from office chairs and sofas to wheelchairs, which are broad claims we would check carefully for your own chair. The text we reviewed does not give the length and width, so confirm the dimensions before ordering.

The side handle is a convenience the 20-inch HAVARGO and TANYOO lack. Compared with the 5 inch HAVARGO it adds an extra inch of lift, and compared with the Zantle at 4 inches it adds two. If your seat is genuinely low and you want the maximum lift in this group, the Acxseo is the one.
products.bestFor: Very low chairs where the maximum height gain is wanted.

products.name: MABOZOO 18x16x6 Inch Extra Thick Booster Cushion
products.description:
The MABOZOO measures 18 by 16 by 6 inches, so it is smaller in footprint than the 20-inch models but just as tall as the Acxseo. The upper layer is memory foam and the lower layer is sponge, wrapped in a breathable air-layer fabric cover. A built-in handle makes it portable, and the cover is separate with a zipper so it can be removed and machine washed.

The smaller 18 by 16 inch footprint fits narrower seats such as dining chairs better than a 20 inch square cushion. The page lists chairs from office and dining to wheelchairs, trucks and cars, claims we would check against your exact seat. The sponge lower layer is the part to watch, since a softer base can compress and lose height sooner than a solid high-density block.

The package arrives compressed and the page suggests beating and shaking it to expand. Compared with the Zantle at 18 by 16 inches and 4 inches thick, it adds two inches of height in the same footprint. If you need a tall, compact cushion for a dining chair or smaller seat, this is the match.

products.name: Zantle 4 Inch Dual-Layer Booster Cushion

specList.label: Layers
specList.value: Firm base foam, softer top layer

products.description:
The Zantle is the shortest cushion in this lineup at 4 inches, sized 18 by 16 inches. A firm, high-elastic base foam holds the elevation while a softer top layer spreads pressure. The maker describes it as an adult booster seat cushion for easier rising, with an anti-slip base that keeps it in place on chairs, sofas and wheelchairs.

The moderate height is the point. For a chair that is only slightly too low, a 4 inch cushion gives a gentler change than 5 or 6 inches and is less likely to leave your feet dangling. The page also lists car seats and wheelchairs, uses we would check against your own seat. The text we reviewed does not describe the cover care, so confirm that on the page.

Compared with the HAVARGO 20 by 20 by 5 inch cushion it is a smaller, lower option, and compared with the MABOZOO at 6 inches it gives a third less lift. If you are unsure how much height you need, starting with the 4 inch Zantle is the cautious route.

buyingCriteria.explanation: Thickness is the whole point of a riser, and more is not always better. The Zantle is 4 inches, the HAVARGO, Hem Dgpsy and TANYOO are 5 inches, and the Acxseo and MABOZOO are 6 inches. A good rule is to raise the seat until your hips sit slightly above your knees while your feet stay flat on the floor. Too much height leaves your feet dangling and can be unsafe, so measure the chair first.

A riser has to stay tall under weight, and that depends on the base foam. The TANYOO and HAVARGO use firm or solid high-density lower layers, the Zantle uses a firm high-elastic base, and the MABOZOO uses sponge under memory foam. A softer base tends to compress sooner. Look for a firm lower layer and a softer top, and expect some settling in the first weeks.

A cushion that hangs over the seat edge can tip or slide. The HAVARGO, Hem Dgpsy and TANYOO are 20 by 20 inches, while the MABOZOO and Zantle are 18 by 16 inches. Measure the usable seat depth and width before choosing. A wide recliner suits the larger squares, and a dining chair suits the smaller rectangles.

A riser that slides is a hazard, because the moment you stand it can shift under you. The HAVARGO and Hem Dgpsy use silicone particles or dots, the TANYOO uses textured silicone dots, and the Acxseo and Zantle list non-slip bottoms. Check that the grip suits your seat fabric, since smooth leather or vinyl is harder to grip. Test by pressing and pushing sideways before relying on it.

Cover care decides how easily the cushion stays fresh. The TANYOO and MABOZOO covers can be machine washed, the Hem Dgpsy waterproof cover is hand wash only, and the HAVARGO has a large zipper opening. The Zantle text we reviewed did not state care. Choose a washable cover for a chair that is used every day.

Most of these arrive compressed, and the height you see out of the box is not the final height. The HAVARGO page asks for 24 hours to expand, the TANYOO suggests a low-heat steamer or hair dryer, and the MABOZOO suggests beating and shaking it. Wait before judging the height. If the cushion never recovers, return it.

howWeEvaluated.title: Height and foam structure
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared stated thickness, from the Zantle at 4 inches to the Acxseo and MABOZOO at 6 inches, and the foam layers used. Firm or solid lower layers on the HAVARGO and TANYOO were rated as a height-retention advantage. We could not measure settling, so these are page-based judgments.

howWeEvaluated.title: Size and fit
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared footprints, with the 20 by 20 inch HAVARGO, Hem Dgpsy and TANYOO against the 18 by 16 inch MABOZOO and Zantle. We considered which chairs each size suits. The Acxseo text did not give dimensions, so we flagged that.

howWeEvaluated.title: Grip and stability
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at the bottom grip on each cushion, including silicone particles, grip dots and non-slip bases. A cushion that shifts under a standing user is a safety issue, so grip carried real weight. We noted which pages say nothing about surface compatibility.

howWeEvaluated.title: Covers and care
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared cover design and washing instructions, from the TANYOO's machine-washable zipper cover to the Hem Dgpsy's hand-wash waterproof cover. Spill protection and ease of removal both counted. We marked where a page gave no care detail.

howWeEvaluated.title: Ownership reality
howWeEvaluated.description: We weighed unpacking and expansion notes, handles and portability, such as the Acxseo's side handle and the MABOZOO's carry handle. Compressed delivery was treated as a normal part of ownership. Value was judged against height and cover features.

faq.q: How thick a riser cushion do I need?
faq.a: Measure the seat height and aim for hips just above knees with feet flat. A slightly low chair suits the 4 inch Zantle, a moderately low one suits a 5 inch cushion like the HAVARGO, and a very low seat may need 6 inches like the Acxseo. Too much height is as risky as too little.

faq.q: Does a riser cushion lift me up when I stand?
faq.a: No. It raises the seat so you start higher, but you still stand with your own leg strength. If you need active help while rising, a lifting cushion or a handle may suit better. A clinician or occupational therapist can advise.

These cushions use silicone particles, dots or non-slip bases to resist sliding, but grip varies with the seat surface. Smooth leather or vinyl is the hardest to grip. Test by pushing sideways before you rely on it. If it moves, do not use it.

faq.q: Why does my cushion look flat out of the box?
faq.a: Most arrive compressed. The HAVARGO page asks for 24 hours to expand, the TANYOO suggests a low-heat steamer or hair dryer, and the MABOZOO suggests beating and shaking it. Give it time before judging the height.

faq.q: Which cover is easiest to wash?
faq.a: The TANYOO cover can be washed by hand or in cold water, and the MABOZOO cover is machine washable. The Hem Dgpsy waterproof cover is hand wash only. Check the care label before washing any cover.

faq.q: Is a riser cushion suitable for a car?
faq.a: Some pages mention car seats, such as the Zantle and MABOZOO. A car seat is contoured and has safety systems, so treat that as a use to check carefully. A different car-focused product may be better.
